prerequisites: Basic mathematical knowledge from the first year.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the terminology and conceptual, logical, and physical models used to represent production systems.
Know the main production configurations and the characteristics of capacity, flow, flexibility, and integration.
Understand the technical and economic criteria for selecting and sizing components and industrial projects.
Know the principles of production planning, inventory management, maintenance, simulation, and digital twin.
Configure and dimension a production system according to product and market characteristics.
Choose and analyze a layout, dimensioning its fundamental elements.
Perform capacity analyses and simple economic evaluations and comparisons between alternatives.
Apply product and machine grouping procedures and interpret simulation and flow monitoring models.
Compare configurations, layouts, and industrial projects based on technical and economic criteria.
Evaluate production constraints and resource performance.
Interpret data related to reliability, failures, and maintenance to guide decisions on production resources.
Describe production systems, models, and indicators with appropriate terminology and illustrate the criteria and evaluations used in the analysis of alternatives.
Develop the ability to integrate knowledge of design, planning, and maintenance of production systems and to independently deepen digital tools for simulation, monitoring, and decision support.

syllabus_topics: Models and data for production: Representation of products, work cycles, resources and orders; data necessary for planning and control of production activities.
Classification of production systems according to material and information flows; capacity, throughput, flexibility, and integration as system characteristics and indicators.
Economic evaluation of machines and industrial projects: Analysis of industrial costs and relationship between costs and production volumes; break-even point.
Determination of the economic value of an industrial machine; present value and main indices for comparative evaluation of industrial projects.
Analysis of production configurations. Layouts by department, in-line, and by cell; product and cycle data necessary for flow study; criteria for comparing configurations.
Group Technology and application of product and machine grouping procedures.

Production planning: Calculation of effective resource capacity, determination of the number of machines, and analysis of production constraints; batch production and comparison between inventory management models.
Role of ERP systems in data sharing and coordination of production, warehouse, and procurement.

Principles of lean production and Just in Time; operation of pull systems and electronic Kanban: consumption acquisition, replenishment signal generation, information update, and flow monitoring between production phases.
Work study and simulation of production flows: Organization of the workstation and association/scheduling between operators and machines.
Introduction to discrete event simulation to represent resource operation and evaluate capacity, waiting times, and utilization levels.
Monitoring and maintenance of resources. Failures, reliability, and operational life of machines; maintenance policies, intervention times, and availability.
Introduction to predictive maintenance with machine state detection techniques, evolution towards machine learning for anomaly recognition and support for maintenance decisions.
Digital twin of production systems: Principles of digital modeling of machines and production processes; connection between the model and data from the physical system.
Use of the digital twin to monitor performance and evaluate operational scenarios.
assessment_rules: The assessment is conducted through an oral examination consisting of three questions, which may cover theoretical aspects or require calculations. Each answer is graded from 0 to 10 points based on correctness, clarity, and depth. The final score, expressed out of thirty, is the sum of the points obtained. A score of 18/30 or higher is required to pass the exam.
